title: Ajvar (Serbian roasted red pepper relish)

ingredients.name: red bell peppers (ideally long red peppers)

steps: Roast the whole peppers and aubergines under a hot grill or in a 230 C oven for 30 to 40 minutes, turning, until the skins are blackened and blistered.
Put the hot vegetables in a covered bowl and let them steam for 20 minutes; this makes peeling much easier.
Peel off the skins, remove the stalks and seeds from the peppers, and scoop the flesh from the aubergines. Drain off excess liquid.
Mince or process the vegetables coarsely, then cook them in a wide, heavy pot with half of the oil, stirring often, for 40 to 60 minutes until thick and dark.
Stir in the remaining oil gradually as the mixture cooks, so it absorbs it, then add the salt, vinegar, and the garlic and chilli if using. Cook a few more minutes.
Cool and serve as a spread or with grilled meat. It keeps for a week in the fridge, or can be sterilised in jars for longer.

title: Česnica (Serbian Christmas coin bread)

ingredients.name: cooled boiled water or still water for brushing (optional)

steps: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in half of the warm water and leave for 10 minutes until it foams.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl, add the yeast mixture, oil and enough of the remaining water to make a soft, elastic dough, and knead for about 10 minutes.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm spot for about an hour until doubled.
Knead the dough briefly and press the foil-wrapped coin into it, then shape it into a round loaf about 24 cm across.
Place it on a lined tray, cover, and let it rise for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan).
Brush the loaf with the egg yolk and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until deep golden brown and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.
Cool on a rack. Traditionally the family breaks the loaf together at the Christmas meal, and whoever finds the coin is said to be lucky for the year.

title: Čvarci (Serbian pork cracklings)

ingredients.name: pork belly or fatty pork trimmings with the skin removed, cut into 2 cm cubes
bread, raw onion and a pickle to serve

steps: Put the pork cubes and the water in a heavy pot over medium heat; the water helps the fat render slowly without scorching.
Cook, stirring from time to time, for about 1 hour. The water will evaporate and the fat will gradually melt out of the meat.
Add the salt, pepper and bay leaf and keep cooking over low heat for another 30 to 40 minutes, stirring, until the pieces are golden brown and crisp and are swimming in clear fat.
Lift the cracklings out with a slotted spoon, pressing them lightly against the pot to release fat, and spread them on kitchen paper. Save the strained fat as lard.
Serve warm or cold with fresh bread, raw onion and pickles, or fold into bread and savoury pastries.

title: Gibanica (Serbian cheese and filo pie)

ingredients.name: white brined cheese (feta or sirene), crumbled
sunflower oil, plus extra for the dish

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan) and oil a large baking tin, about 25 by 35 cm.
Beat the eggs with the yogurt, sparkling water and oil, then stir in the crumbled cheese and pepper. Taste before adding salt as the cheese is salty.
Layer 3 filo sheets in the tin, spreading a few spoonfuls of the egg-cheese mixture over them, and repeat, using a little less mixture in each layer.
When you have used up all the pastry, pour any remaining mixture over the top and tuck in the edges.
Cut the pie into squares before baking, so it cuts neatly later, then bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Cover with a clean cloth for 10 minutes, which softens the top, then serve warm with yogurt.

title: Karađorđeva šnicla (Serbian rolled cutlet stuffed with kajmak)

ingredients.name: pork or veal cutlets (about 150 g each), pounded thin
kajmak (or clotted cream, or mascarpone mixed with a pinch of salt)
lemon wedges, tartar sauce and chips to serve

steps: Lay the cutlets between sheets of cling film and pound them very thin, about 5 mm, then season with salt and pepper.
Spoon a line of kajmak onto the centre of each cutlet and roll it up tightly, folding in the sides so the filling cannot leak. Secure with a toothpick if needed.
Chill the rolls for 30 minutes so they hold their shape.
Dredge each roll in flour, dip it in beaten egg, and coat it fully in breadcrumbs, pressing so they stick.
Heat the oil to about 170 C in a deep pan and fry the rolls for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve whole or sliced, with lemon, tartar sauce and chips.

title: Knedle sa šljivama (Serbian plum dumplings)

ingredients.name: floury potatoes, boiled in their skins
plain flour, plus extra for dusting
sugar cubes, or 1 tsp sugar for each plum

steps: Peel the boiled potatoes while still warm and mash them smooth. Let them cool, then mix in the flour, egg and salt and knead lightly into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Cut the plums open along one side to remove the stone, and put a sugar cube in each plum.
Roll the dough out to about 5 mm thick and cut it into squares large enough to wrap a plum. Wrap each plum fully, and roll it between your palms into a smooth ball.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil and add the dumplings in batches, so they are not crowded. Cook for about 10 minutes, until they float and are cooked through.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a pan, add the breadcrumbs and the 3 tablespoons of sugar and fry until golden and fragrant, then stir in the cinnamon.
Lift the dumplings out with a slotted spoon, roll them in the crumbs and serve warm.

title: Krofne (Serbian jam-filled doughnuts)

ingredients.name: apricot jam or other thick jam

steps: Stir the yeast and a pinch of the sugar into the warm milk and leave for 10 minutes until it foams.
Mix the flour, the rest of the sugar, salt and lemon zest, then add the yeast milk, egg yolks, butter and rum, and knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let the dough rise, covered, for about an hour until doubled. Roll out to 1.5 cm thick and cut rounds about 7 cm across.
Place the rounds on a floured cloth, cover, and let them rise for another 30 minutes until puffy.
Heat the oil to 170 C and fry the krofne for 2 to 3 minutes per side, covered for the first side so they stay pale around the middle, until golden.
Drain, cool slightly, then use a piping bag with a narrow nozzle to inject jam into the side of each one. Dust with icing sugar.

title: Leskovačka mućkalica (Serbian pork and pepper stew)

ingredients.name: pork neck, cut into 3 cm cubes
red peppers, roasted, peeled and sliced

steps: Render the bacon in the lard over medium heat in a heavy pot, then add the pork and sear it on high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until browned all over.
Add the onions and cook, stirring, until soft and golden, then add the garlic.
Sprinkle in the flour and paprika and stir for about 2 minutes, taking care not to scorch the paprika.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the roasted peppers, tomatoes, stock, bay leaf, salt and pepper.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 1 to 1.5 hours, until the pork is tender and the sauce is thick.
Serve with rice, cornbread or fresh bread, and a salad.

title: Pasulj (Serbian bean stew with smoked pork)

ingredients.name: smoked pork ribs or ham hock
dried hot pepper or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes (optional)

steps: Drain the soaked beans, put them in a large pot with fresh water, bring to a boil for 5 minutes, then drain and discard the water.
Return the beans to the pot with the smoked meat, carrots, half of the onion, the bay leaves and enough fresh water to cover by 5 cm.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 1 to 1.5 hours until the beans are tender and the meat is nearly falling off the bone.
In a separate pan, heat the oil and fry the remaining onion until golden, add the garlic, flour and paprika and stir for 1 minute to make a roux.
Ladle in some bean broth to loosen the roux, then stir it into the pot and simmer for another 15 to 20 minutes until the stew is thick.
Season with salt and pepper (the smoked meat may already be salty), and serve hot with bread, raw onion and sour cream or ajvar.

title: Pinđur (Serbian pepper, tomato and aubergine spread)
steps: Roast the peppers and aubergine under a hot grill, turning, until they are blackened all over, then put them in a covered bowl to steam for 15 minutes.
Peel the peppers and aubergine, remove the seeds and stalks, and chop the flesh finely.
Blanch the tomatoes in boiling water for a minute, peel them, and chop them, draining off the excess juice.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot, add the vegetables with the salt and sugar, and simmer uncovered for about 40 minutes, stirring often, until the mixture is thick and chunky.
Stir in the garlic and vinegar and cook for 5 more minutes. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve warm or cold as a spread on bread, or with grilled meats; it is chunkier than ajvar.

title: Pljeskavica (Serbian grilled meat patty)

ingredients.name: chopped raw onion, kajmak (or clotted cream) and ajvar to serve

steps: Mix the beef, pork, onion, garlic, salt, pepper, paprika and baking soda in a large bowl.
Knead the meat for 4 to 5 minutes, adding the water gradually, until the mixture is sticky and holds together; this helps the patties stay juicy.
Cover and chill for at least an hour so the flavours blend and the meat firms up.
With wet hands, divide the mixture into 4 and press each portion into a flat patty about 15 cm across and 1.5 cm thick.
Cook on a hot grill or griddle for 5 to 6 minutes per side, pressing lightly with a spatula only at the start, until cooked through and well browned.
Toast the flatbreads on the grill for a minute, then fill with the patties, chopped raw onion, a spoonful of kajmak and ajvar.

title: Podvarak (Serbian baked sauerkraut with pork)

ingredients.name: pork shoulder or leftover roast pork, in large pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan). Season the pork with salt and brown it in a hot pan with half of the fat, then set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion in the remaining fat until golden, then stir in the paprika and take the pan off the heat.
In a deep baking dish, mix the sauerkraut with the onion mixture, bay leaves, peppercorns and rice if using.
Tuck the pork pieces into the sauerkraut, pour in the water, and cover tightly with foil or a lid.
Bake for about 2 hours, until the pork is very tender and the cabbage has softened and mellowed.
Uncover for the last 15 minutes to lightly brown the top, then serve hot with potatoes or bread.

title: Prebranac (Serbian baked beans with onions)

ingredients.name: dried white beans (large, such as butter beans), soaked overnight
dried hot pepper or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes

steps: Drain the beans, cover with fresh water and simmer for about 45 to 60 minutes until nearly tender, but not falling apart. Drain, keeping about 300 ml of the cooking water.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onions slowly for 20 minutes, stirring, until very soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and hot pepper for a minute, then take the pan off the heat so the paprika does not burn.
Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan). In a baking dish or clay pot, mix the beans with the onion mixture, bay leaves, salt and the reserved cooking water.
Bake uncovered for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until the beans are creamy inside and the top has a sticky, caramelised crust.
Serve warm or at room temperature with bread and a pickled vegetable salad.

title: Ražnjići (Serbian pork skewers)

ingredients.name: pork neck or shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
bread or lepinja and ajvar to serve

steps: Put the pork in a bowl with the grated onion, oil, paprika, salt and pepper, and mix well.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 3 hours, or overnight.
If you use wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes. Thread the meat onto the skewers, packing the cubes closely.
Heat a grill or griddle until very hot and cook the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning regularly, until browned and cooked through but still juicy.
Serve at once on warm bread with sliced raw onion and a spoonful of ajvar.

title: Ruske kape (Serbian chocolate and walnut "Russian caps")

ingredients.name: dark chocolate, melted, for the topping

steps: Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, adding the sugar gradually, then fold in the walnuts, flour and half of the vanilla. Bake as small rounds or in a tin at 170 C (150 C fan) for about 20 minutes until springy, then cool and cut into small rounds.

Whisk a little of the cold milk with the custard powder, bring the rest of the milk to a boil, stir in the paste and cook for a couple of minutes until thick. Cool completely with cling film on the surface.
Beat the butter with the icing sugar until fluffy, then beat in the cooled custard and the remaining vanilla to make a smooth cream.
Place a round of cake on a plate, spread with cream, and add another layer, building up small stacks.
Coat the sides of each stack with cream and roll the sides in coconut.
Spoon melted chocolate over the tops and chill for at least an hour before serving.

title: Šampita (Serbian meringue and custard slice)
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, then mix in the egg yolks, 1 tablespoon sugar and sour cream to make a soft dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan). Roll the dough out to fit a baking tray lined with baking paper and bake for about 15 minutes until pale golden. Let it cool.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoonful at a time, whisking until the meringue is stiff and glossy.
Spread the meringue over the baked base and bake at 120 C (100 C fan) for 40 to 50 minutes, until dry and just starting to colour. Cool completely.
Whip the cream with the vanilla until it holds soft peaks and spread it over the meringue.
Chill for a couple of hours, then cut into squares with a hot knife.

title: Sataraš (Serbian pepper, tomato and onion stew)

ingredients.name: green or red bell peppers, cut into strips

steps: Warm the oil in a wide pan and cook the onions over medium heat for about 8 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the pepper strips and fry for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tomatoes, paprika, salt and sugar, then cover and simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes, until the vegetables are very soft and the juices are thick.
If you want to add eggs, make two wells in the stew, break the eggs into them, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, or stir them in to scramble.
Serve warm or cold with bread, or as a side with grilled meat or sausages.

title: Slavski kolač (Serbian ritual slava bread)
steps: Mix the yeast with the sugar and a few spoonfuls of the warm water and leave until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, add the yeast, oil and the rest of the water, and knead for 10 minutes into a smooth, soft dough.
Let it rise, covered, until doubled, about 1 to 1.5 hours.
Divide off about a quarter of the dough, and shape the rest into a round loaf. Roll the smaller piece into strips and shape a cross, a braid or small decorations to place on top.
Set the loaf on a lined tray and press the decoration gently on top. Let it rise again for 30 minutes.
Brush with egg yolk and bake at 190 C (170 C fan) for 35 to 45 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding.
Cool on a rack. For the slava, the loaf is blessed, wine is poured over it and the family cuts or breaks it together before the meal.

title: Srpska salata (Serbian tomato, cucumber and pepper salad)

ingredients.name: fresh or pickled hot pepper, sliced (optional)

steps: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, onion and bell pepper in a large bowl.
Add the hot pepper if using, then sprinkle the salt over and toss gently so the vegetables release some juice.
Dress with the oil and vinegar and toss again.
Scatter with parsley and serve right away, with grilled meat, ćevapi or pljeskavica, and bread to mop up the dressing.

title: Svadbarski kupus (Serbian wedding cabbage)

ingredients.name: mixed pork and smoked pork (shoulder, smoked ribs), in large pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 160 C (140 C fan). Rinse the sauerkraut briefly if it is very sour and squeeze out some of the liquid.
In a large, deep pot or clay crock, scatter some of the bacon and onion on the bottom, then add a layer of sauerkraut, then a layer of meat, and a sprinkle of paprika and peppercorns.
Repeat the layers until everything is used, finishing with a layer of cabbage and tucking in the bay leaves.
Pour in enough water to just cover the top layer, cover tightly and bring to a simmer on the stove.
Transfer to the oven and cook for 3.5 to 4 hours, without stirring, until the meat is tender and the cabbage is sweet and soft; add a little more water if it looks dry.
Taste before adding any salt, then serve hot with bread. As with many stews, it tastes even better the next day.

title: Tulumbe (Serbian syrup-soaked fried dough fingers)

ingredients.name: lemon, a few slices or the juice of half

steps: Make the syrup first: boil the sugar, water and lemon for about 10 minutes until it is lightly thickened, then let it cool completely.
Bring the water, butter and salt for the dough to a boil, tip in all the flour at once and stir hard until the dough comes away from the pan in a smooth ball.
Cool the dough for 10 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until it is smooth and glossy.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag with a large star nozzle, and heat the oil to about 170 C.
Pipe 6 to 8 cm lengths directly into the hot oil, cutting them with scissors, and fry for about 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp.
Lift out onto kitchen paper for a moment, then drop the hot tulumbe into the cold syrup and soak them for a minute.
Lift them out onto a rack to drain and serve at room temperature.

title: Urnebes (Serbian spicy cheese salad from Niš)

ingredients.name: kajmak, or clotted cream or mascarpone
hot red pepper (or 1 to 2 tsp hot ground red pepper)

steps: Mash the crumbled cheese with a fork until it is mostly smooth with a few small lumps.
Stir in the kajmak until the mixture is creamy and spreadable.
Finely chop the fresh peppers, removing the seeds if you want it milder, and fold them in, or stir in the ground hot pepper.
Add the garlic if using, then beat in the oil a spoonful at a time.
Taste, adjust the heat, and chill for 30 minutes so the flavours settle.
Serve with grilled meat such as pljeskavica or ćevapi, or spread on bread, topped with parsley.

title: Uštipci (Serbian fried dough balls)

ingredients.name: kajmak, jam, honey or crumbled white cheese to serve

steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave it for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl, add the egg, 2 tablespoons of oil and the yeast milk, and mix to a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the frying oil to about 175 C in a deep pan. Wet two spoons or your hands and scoop out walnut-sized pieces of dough.
Fry the dough balls in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until puffed and deep golden, and cooked through.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve warm with kajmak and white cheese for a savoury version, or with jam or honey.
